english.title: Wear / otherwise use item to conceal identity at a protest
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in a public place within a locality designated under section 158 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026,

(A)_[wore an item, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ITEM..)]_
(B)_[used an item, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ITEM AND MANNER USED..)]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 157 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026.

english.notes:
(i) “Public place” has the meaning given by section 16 of the Public Order Act 1986. (ii) Section 157(2) provides a defence for a person charged with this offence where the individual can prove that they wore or otherwise used the item for a purpose relating to the health of the person or others, religious observance, or a purpose relating to the person’s work. The burden is on the defendant to prove the defence. (iii) See section 60AA of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 - power to require removal of disguises. (iv) Reference to “otherwise using an item” is to ensure the offence applies not only to face coverings, but also other items. The term is not further defined but, in the opinion of PNLD, this would cover items such as placards or masks held close to the face when used for the purpose of concealing identity.(v) This offence may only be committed within the specified 24-hour period of a designation under section 158(1) where a constable designating the locality has ensured all reasonable steps were taken to notify the public of the designation being made, the nature of this offence, the locality to which the designation applies and the period the designation is in force. It will be for the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that such reasonable steps were taken (section 157(3)).
(vi) This offence may only be committed within a 24-hour extension period of a designation via section 158(3) where the public have been notified the designation will continue in force, the nature of this offence, the locality to which the designation applies and the period the designation is in force. Again, it is for the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that such reasonable steps were taken (sections 157(4) and 158(4)).
